sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Union City, NJ?
sections.html:
A cash sale to a buyer who takes the building as-is is the quickest way out in Union City, because the buyer absorbs the city's sale-of-property letter and any repair list. Listing with an agent can still bring a strong price for a clean two-family or a condo, and owners may sell on their own, but each path ends at the Building Department for the same letter.

The Census Bureau estimates 66,656 residents for mid-2025, a 2.9% drop from the 2020 estimates base of 68,641. All of them live on 1.29 square miles of land, a 2020 density of 53,293.7 people per square mile, which is among the highest in the country.

sections.h2: Where is Union City, and how did it come together?
sections.html:
Union City is in the northern part of Hudson County, on the ridge of the Palisades with views toward the Manhattan skyline and the Meadowlands. It was incorporated on June 1, 1925, when Union Hill and West Hoboken merged. German immigrants built the lace and embroidery trade that earned the city the nickname "Embroidery Capital of the United States," and Cuban arrivals from the late 1940s onward gave it the other nickname, "Havana on the Hudson."

The city touches Hoboken, Jersey City, North Bergen, Weehawken and West New York, and it is the only Hudson County municipality completely surrounded by other municipalities in the county. Route 495, the approach to the Lincoln Tunnel, cuts through it, and Kennedy Boulevard forms most of the western edge. Street grids run on numbers, with 49th Street at the northern line and Paterson Plank Road along the southern border with Jersey City.

  • The former West Hoboken section lies south of 32nd Street and overlooks Hoboken.
  • The former Union Hill section lies north of it and runs up to the West New York line.
  • Bergenline Avenue is the main shopping street and the main bus corridor.
  • Reservoir Park on Palisade Avenue between 20th and 22nd Streets opened in 2015.

sections.h2: What are Union City homes worth, and who owns them?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 Census data show a median owner-occupied value of $471,600 and median gross rent of $1,537. Only 19.1% of the city's 25,725 households own their home, so most buildings are rented and a typical seller owns a two- to six-family house or a condo. Owners with a mortgage carry a median of $3,088 a month in housing costs.

Median household income is $64,310 and 23.1% of residents are in poverty. About 54.3% were born outside the United States and 81.8% of residents age five and over speak a language other than English at home. The city posts its forms in English and Spanish.

sections.h2: What does Union City require before a house is sold?
sections.html:
Union City asks for a Sale of Property letter from the Building Department before a sale. The application form names the owner, buyer, building type and number of units, and a mandatory lead inspection must be completed before the letter is issued. The letter is good for 60 days after issuance, so a seller who is slow to close may need to renew.

The Building Department also posts a Certificate of Occupancy Exemption Letter, an Application for Inspection Approval Certificate, a Certification of Continued Use form and a procedure for legalizing non-conforming basement units. A basement apartment that was never permitted is the item that most often slows a Union City closing, so ask the Building Department what it will take to legalize or remove one before you list.

sections.h2: How do rent control and landlord registration affect a Union City sale?
sections.html:
The city's forms page lists a rent control program with an annual registration statement, a legal rent request form, capital improvement and hardship applications, and a landlord and tenant inquiry form. A buyer of a rented building will want the current registration and the legal rent for each unit, so the seller should gather them early.

Other filings come up in the same transaction.

  • A registration form for multiple dwellings and a Multiple Dwelling Green Card.
  • A Landlord Identity Statement filed with the City Clerk.
  • A registration of vacant and abandoned properties, and a separate registration form for properties in foreclosure.
  • A request form for a rebuild letter after a fire or similar loss.

An empty building is therefore not a simple exit. If you hold a vacant house, ask the Building Department which registrations apply before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: How are Union City property taxes billed, and what is a reassessment?
sections.html:
The city bills in quarters due on February 1, May 1, August 1 and November 1. Overdue amounts carry interest of 8% a year up to $1,500 and 18% a year above that, and the city allows 10 calendar days from the original due date only if bills were mailed on time. A municipal lien still unpaid on November 11 can go to tax sale, and anything in lien must be paid with certified funds.

The Tax Department site also carries a reassessment presentation and a reassessment FAQ, both in English and Spanish, a state revaluation order, a lookup for assessments and instructions for appealing a property value. Senior Freeze applications and a 5 Year Tax Abatement application are posted there too. Hand the new owner the current tax bill at closing and ask the department for a duplicate if you cannot find it.

sections.h2: What drives Union City's economy and buyer interest?
sections.html:
Bergenline Avenue is the center of local commerce. It began as a narrow cowpath, became the trolley route in the 19th century, and grew into one of the longest commercial avenues in the state, with its main retail stretch beginning at 32nd Street and running north into North Bergen. At the southern end, shopping gathers around Summit Avenue and the old Transfer Station, where the city rebuilt sidewalks and lighting from 7th to 13th Street in 2009.

Embroidery faded as a trade by the late 1990s, and the city dedicated Embroidery Square on New York Avenue in 2014 to mark it. Union City is also one of the Hudson County cities with a state-established Urban Enterprise Zone. Retail sales in 2022 were $434,135,000, or $6,706 per resident, per the Census Bureau, and health care and social assistance receipts were $209,773,000.

sections.h2: How do roads, schools and transit shape demand in Union City?
sections.html:
Union City has about 41.67 miles of roads, most of them maintained by the city. Route 495 leads to the Lincoln Tunnel, and the Hudson-Bergen Light Rail stops at 49th Street near the West New York and North Bergen lines. New Jersey Transit buses serve the city with routes to the Port Authority Bus Terminal in Midtown Manhattan, the George Washington Bridge Bus Terminal and Jersey City.

The Union City School District, a former Abbott district, enrolled 12,848 students in 14 schools in 2022-23. The main green space is Washington Park, a 22-acre county park on the Jersey City line, and the 14.4-acre Reservoir Park. Median travel to work is 33.1 minutes, and 28.3% of adults hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

faqs.q: What letter does Union City require to sell a house?
faqs.a: A Sale of Property letter from the Building Department, which costs $100 to process and requires a mandatory lead inspection first. The letter is good for 60 days after issuance.

faqs.q: How much is the lead inspection in Union City?
faqs.a: The city's sale-of-property form lists $120 per unit for one to four units and $220 per unit for five or more, directly under the lead inspection note. Ask the Building Department to confirm what applies to your building when you apply.

faqs.q: What are the Union City tax due dates?
faqs.a: Taxes are due on the first of February, May, August and November. Interest is 8% up to $1,500 of delinquency and 18% on the amount above that.

faqs.q: Does rent control follow the building when I sell in Union City?
faqs.a: The rent control program applies to covered rental units, so the buyer takes the building with its registration and legal rents. Gather the annual registration statement and legal rent records before you list.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Union City house with an unpermitted basement apartment?
faqs.a: It can sell, usually to a cash buyer, but the Building Department publishes a procedure for legalizing non-conforming basement units and open issues can delay the sale letter. Ask the department what applies to your building before you go to market.
